message.content:
Here are some practical tips to keep your piano in top shape: | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |-----|----------------|--------------| | **Keep it at the right humidity** | Pianos expand and contract with moisture; too dry or too wet can warp wood and damage strings. | • Use a hygrometer inside the piano.
• Maintain 45‑55 % RH (relative humidity).
• In dry climates, use a humidifier; in damp areas, use a dehumidifier. | | **Dust regularly** | Dust can accumulate on the soundboard and inside the action, affecting tone and playability. | • Wipe the exterior with a soft, dry cloth.
• Use a vacuum with a soft brush attachment for the interior. | | **Tune periodically** | Tuning keeps the piano sounding correct and prevents long‑term damage from out‑of‑tune strings. | • Schedule a professional tuning every 3–6 months (more often if you play daily). | | **Check the action** | Loose hammers or worn felt reduce touch response and tone. | • Have a technician inspect the action annually.
• Replace worn parts as recommended. | | **Avoid direct sunlight** | UV rays fade finish and can cause uneven drying. | • Keep the piano away from windows or use curtains/UV‑blocking film. | | **Control temperature** | Rapid temperature changes can stress the wood and metal. | • Keep the room at a stable 65–75 °F (18–24 °C). | | **Use a piano cover** | Covers protect against dust, pets, and accidental spills. | • Store a clean, breathable cover when the piano isn’t in use. | | **Prevent pests** | Wood‑boring insects can damage the soundboard. | • Inspect for signs of infestation.
• Use safe pest deterrents if needed. | | **Professional servicing** | A technician can spot issues before they become costly problems. | • Schedule a full service every 1–2 years. | If you’re unsure about any part of maintenance, a qualified piano technician can give you personalized advice and perform routine services. Happy playing!
